stem.text: Does the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{\left(n + 6\right) \left(n + 7\right)} \) converge? If it does, find its sum.

answer_key.label: The series converges, and its sum is \( \frac{1}{7} \).

worked_solution.text: Each term splits as \( \frac{1}{\left(n + 6\right) \left(n + 7\right)} = \frac{1}{n + 6} - \frac{1}{n + 7} \), so in the nth partial sum every middle term cancels and \( S_n = \frac{1}{7} - \frac{1}{n + 7} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: partial sums of a telescoping series

worked_solution.text: A series converges exactly when its partial sums approach a finite limit. Here \( \lim_{n \to \infty} S_n = \frac{1}{7} \), so the series converges and its sum is \( \frac{1}{7} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: convergence as the limit of the partial sums
